sheet-2.description: The north end of Edgewater at the Fort Lee boundary, drawn at 50 ft to an inch. River Road enters at the top from Fort Lee, bends below the boundary and runs south down the middle of the sheet to Hudson Place at the bottom. Along the top runs the boundary line between Fort Lee and Edgewater, between Delafolie Place on the Fort Lee side and Massa's Lane on the Edgewater side; block 65 beyond it belongs to Fort Lee, and a second Fort Lee boundary line runs along the hillside at the lower left. West of River Road the ground rises as a steep hillside to the top of the high bluff; Leary Lane and an unnamed lane run up from River Road into large lots with scattered frame dwellings, sheds and a plastered dwelling. At the bottom Hudson Place turns off River Road and runs north as a 20 ft lane, framing a block of narrow lots with dwellings, the Edgewater Cut Glass Works and the Hudson Villa Hotel at the corner of River Road. East of River Road a few large lots and one dwelling lie between it and Annett Avenue, a 60 ft avenue drawn curving through open ground on the right of the sheet, laid out but with no buildings along it. A 12 inch water pipe runs in River Road with hydrants, and a note at the bend records the Englewood standpipe pressure; 6 inch pipes run in Hudson Place. House numbers are given along River Road, and the block numbers of the borough key (1 to 13, 65) are printed on the blocks.
notes: Hudson Place is modern Maple Street (east-west arm) and the north end of Undercliff Avenue (north-south arm); Massa's Lane is modern Massa Lane; the unnamed lane between Leary Lane and Hudson Place is modern Hooks Lane.
Annett Avenue is not in the modern street data; the private roads of the Edgewater Colony now cover the ground east of River Road.
Hudson Place / River Road read by hand was 8 m off the fit and is not used; the modern Maple Street junction does not match the drawn one closely.
50 ft. River Road from the Fort Lee line (Massa's Lane) to Hudson Pl.; Leary Lane, unnamed lane (Hooks Lane), Annett Av. (gone). One part; 4 GCPs (3 auto, Leary/River hand-picked).

sheet-3.description: The north end of Edgewater on River Road between Hudson Place and Maple, drawn at 50 ft to an inch. River Road runs down the right-centre of the sheet; at the top Hudson Place crosses from River Road to its short north-south arm, and Annett Avenue branches off River Road to the north-east. West of River Road long narrow lots (blocks 15 to 20) climb the steep hillside towards the top of the high bluff and the Fort Lee boundary line at the left, with frame dwellings, sheds and a wagon shed near the road. Lower down Palisade Terrace, a 50 ft street, runs from River Road into blocks 21 and 22 divided into small numbered lots, mostly vacant; at its corner on River Road stands Fire Department Fire Co. No. 1 with a bell tower, housing a hook and ladder truck and a hose cart, beside a store. At the bottom, Undercliff Avenue begins at Maple, with Public School No. 2 (heated by furnace, electric light) on block 25 and dwellings on block 27. East of River Road the ground down to the Hudson River is drawn as three large undivided lots (A, B and C) with no buildings except a shed and a small saw mill with a 35 horsepower steam engine on the shore. Water pipes are marked in River Road (12 inch), Hudson Place and Palisade Terrace (6 inch), with hydrants; house numbers are given along River Road and the block numbers of the borough key (11 to 27) are printed on the blocks.
notes: Hudson Place is modern Maple Street (east-west) and the north end of Undercliff Avenue (north-south arm, a 20 ft lane, too narrow for the detector).

Modern Palisade Terrace lies about 19 m south of the drawn Palisade Terrace, and modern Undercliff Avenue now runs straight through drawn blocks 22 and 24 to join the old Undercliff Avenue at Maple; neither was used as control.
The drawn Maple is not in the modern street data. The bottom of the sheet is placed from block corners carried from sheet 4.
Fitted scale is about 2 percent larger than on sheets 2 and 4 (8.05 against 7.9 px/ft).

50 ft. River Road from Hudson Pl. to Maple; Palisade Ter. (modern one 19 m south), Fire Co. No. 1, Public School No. 2. One part; placed by one hand-picked junction and three block corners carried from sheets 2 and 4.

sheet-4.description: The residential north end of Edgewater between the foot of the Palisades and the Hudson River, drawn at 50 ft to an inch. Undercliff Avenue runs down the left side of the sheet below a steep hillside, and River Road runs down the right, curving towards the shore at the bottom; Maple (at the top edge), Orchard Place, Park (marked not opened) and Sterling Place cross between them, and Lasher's Lane turns off River Road into the block south of Park. The blocks are laid out in narrow numbered lots, mostly vacant; the built lots carry frame dwellings of two and two and a half storeys, with garages, sheds and wagon sheds. Along Undercliff Avenue at Sterling Place stands the First Presbyterian Church (heated by furnace, electric light). East of River Road the ground falls to the river as large undivided lots with a few dwellings, garages and sheds; the shore line is drawn with a pier on piles at the top, a boat house on piles in the middle and the Edgewater Yacht Club boat house on poles at the bottom right. Water pipes are marked in the streets: a 12 inch main in River Road and 6 inch pipes in Undercliff Avenue and Sterling Place, with hydrants. Lot numbers on the blocks and house numbers along the street fronts are given throughout, and the block numbers of the borough key (27 to 42) are printed on the blocks.
notes: Maple, the street along the top edge, is not in the modern street data; modern Maple Street lies about 300 m further north. Washington Lane meets River Road near its east end.
Park (not opened in 1911) is modern Park Street; Orchard Place is modern Orchard Street; Lasher's Lane is modern Lasher Lane.
River Road is drawn about 30 ft wide, against 45 to 58 ft for the modern right-of-way.
50 ft. Undercliff Av. and River Road, Maple to Sterling Pl.; Orchard Pl., Park (Park Street), Lasher's Lane. One part; pilot, 6 auto GCPs with default detector.

sheet-5.description: A residential subdivision in the middle of Edgewater between the hillside and River Road, drawn at 50 ft to an inch. North Street crosses the top of the sheet diagonally from the hillside to River Road. Below it three parallel streets run down the sheet: Glenwood Avenue on the left, curving south-east at the bottom into a cross street that runs to River Road; Myrtle Avenue in the middle; and River Road on the right. Rockwood Place leaves the junction of Glenwood and Myrtle avenues towards the south-west. Blocks 47, 48, 49, 51 and 52 are cut into long rows of narrow numbered lots, most still vacant, with frame dwellings of two to two and a half storeys, many with open first storeys, on the occupied lots, and a church on Rockwood Place. North of North Street lies the large block 43 with a few dwellings and an outhouse at the top. East of River Road, on the river side, stand the Hotel Buena Vista with a wagon shed and shed (block 44), a dwelling and shed on solid filling, and two piers on piles enclosing a basin of the Hudson River; at the bottom right is the repair shop of the Iron Steam Boat Co. A steep hillside forms the left edge. Water pipes are marked in the streets (6 inch in the subdivision streets, 12 inch in River Road) with hydrants, and house numbers are given along River Road.
notes: The north-south part of Glenwood Avenue is now part of Undercliff Avenue; the curved lower part and the cross street to River Road keep the name Glenwood Avenue.
The two bottom junctions (Glenwood / Myrtle, Glenwood / River Road) are hand-picked: the curved street defeats the detector. Residuals are 3 to 6 m, larger than on neighbouring sheets.
Hotel Buena Vista on River Road; Iron Steam Boat Co. repair shop on the shore.
50 ft. North St., Glenwood Av. (N-S part now Undercliff Av.), Myrtle Av., Rockwood Pl., River Road. One part; 3 auto + 2 hand-picked on the curved Glenwood Av.

sheet-6.description: The part of Edgewater where Bluff Road climbs from River Road to the top of the Palisades, drawn at 50 ft to an inch and turned on the sheet so that north points to the upper right. River Road runs diagonally across the lower half along the Hudson River shore. Bluff Road leaves River Road at the lower left, runs parallel to it up to Undercliff Avenue, and then turns in a hairpin loop up the hillside to the top of the high bluff and the Fort Lee boundary line at the top of the sheet. Undercliff Avenue crosses the upper part of the sheet, and Valley Place runs from it down to Bluff Road. The blocks between the streets (59, 60, 61 and 63) are cut into narrow numbered lots with frame dwellings of two to two and a half storeys, a stuccoed flat, a studio and a stone dwelling on the hillside, and three-family flats along River Road at the upper right. Public School No. 3 (steam heat) stands on Undercliff Avenue at Valley Place. On the river side of Bluff Road are R. E. Ward's shell boat builder's shop, the Fulton Garage, the Hudson Dye Works with its washing, storage and steam rooms and naphtha stores, the Geisen Cleaning Co., and the Edgewater Casino with bowling alleys and dancing on the second floor. Across River Road on the shore are a blacksmith shop, the Edgewater Lumber Co. at the lower left, piers on piles and a long pier reaching into the river. Water pipes (6 and 12 inch) are marked in the streets with hydrants, and house numbers are given along River Road and Bluff Road.
notes: The lower straight part of Bluff Road is modern Hudson Terrace; the hairpin loop up the bluff is now State Route 5. Valley Place is modern Valley Terrace.

Only one street junction survives in usable form (Undercliff Avenue / Valley Terrace); the part is placed mainly by four block corners matched to modern parcel corners (blocks 60 and 63, whose outlines survive almost unchanged).
The modern State Route 5 / Undercliff Avenue node and the east tip of block 60 sit about 8 m off the fit; the route junction was left out.
Fitted scale about 3 percent larger than nominal (8.13 against about 7.9 px/ft).

50 ft, turned (north to upper right, about 62 deg). Bluff Road (lower part = Hudson Terrace, loop = Route 5), Undercliff Av., Valley Pl. (Valley Terrace), River Road. One part; placed by block corners matched to modern parcels.

sheet-7.description: The Edgewater terminus of the Public Service Railway and the Fort Lee ferry, on River Road between Dempsey Avenue and Bluff Road, drawn at 50 ft to an inch and turned on the sheet so that north points to the upper right. At the top left Undercliff Avenue crosses the corner, with three pairs of two and a half storey dwellings on block 67 and the street railroad right of way beyond them. Dempsey Avenue runs down the left side from Undercliff Avenue to River Road, with Columbia Terrace East leaving it to the west, and the Public Service Railway runs beside it. On block 65 stand the railway's car barn and repair shop (cement floors, steel trusses, sky lights, offices and store room, a blacksmith shop, paint storage and oil houses) and its power house with dynamos, engines, turbines and a boiler house beside a coal pile, with notes on watchmen, power, heating and fire appliances. Along River Road are a saloon, a hose cart house, a lunch cart, a soda fountain, the entrance to Palisade Amusement Park, a hotel, saloon and hall and an auto garage; the rest of the large block 64, up to Bluff Road at the right edge, is open ground divided into lots 1 and 2 with a few sheds. Below River Road, on block 66 on the Hudson River, is the ferry house of the Public Service Railway with its waiting room, offices, employees' waiting room and work shop, two ferry slips for the ferry to 130th Street, New York, a coal pier on piles and two further piers on piles. A 12 inch water pipe runs in River Road and a 6 inch pipe in Dempsey Avenue, with hydrants and a fire alarm box at the ferry house.
notes: Placed by two detected junctions on Dempsey Avenue (Undercliff Avenue, River Road) and one block corner at the Bluff Road end of River Road carried from sheet 6; three points, no redundancy.
Modern Hudson Avenue does not follow any drawn street on this sheet (it runs through the open block 64); Columbia Terrace / Dempsey Avenue read by hand was 8 m off and is not used.
Ferry to 130th Street, New York, from the Public Service Railway ferry house; Palisade Amusement Park entrance on River Road.

50 ft, turned like sheet 6. Dempsey Av., Undercliff Av., River Road; Public Service Railway car barn, power house and ferry house, Palisade Amusement Park entrance. One part; 3 points (2 auto on Dempsey, 1 carried from sheet 6).

sheet-8.description: The centre of Edgewater around the Hilliard Avenue crossing, drawn at 50 ft to an inch with north about 24 degrees anticlockwise of up. Undercliff Avenue runs down the left side below the steep hillside, Edgewater Place down the middle and River Road down the right, with the Hudson River beyond it. Dempsey Avenue crosses the top of the sheet, Columbia Terrace East and Columbia Terrace South form an L around block 69, and Hilliard Avenue (lettered Hillard Av.) crosses the middle. The blocks west of Undercliff Avenue (68, 75, 82) and blocks 69, 76 and 81 hold rows of two and two and a half storey frame dwellings and a few flats. The commercial centre lies on Dempsey Avenue and River Road: the First National Bank and the post office at Columbia Terrace East, stores, a drug store and bank office, a hotel and saloon, and the Francis Derveaux cleaning and dyeing works on block 70. On block 73 at River Road stands the Municipal Building, which also houses the fire department (Hook and Ladder No. 2, Hose Company No. 2). Block 77 has stores, a barber, saloon and restaurant, a bakery, plumbing and paint shops and club rooms, and at its south end the Edgewater Hygeia Ice Company ice plant and the yarn dyeing works of D. A. Higgins and Co. East of River Road (block 71 and 78) are a few stores, an insurance office and an oil and paint store, a large building at the top right, and the river shore with a pier at the bottom. The lower part of the sheet below the dyeing works is mostly blank, belonging to sheet 9. Water pipes of 6 and 12 inches run in the streets.
notes: Hillard Avenue on the sheet is modern Hilliard Avenue.
Columbia Terrace East and Columbia Terrace South are both part of modern Columbia Terrace.
Per-part detector setting ink_below_paper 100: with the atlas default (138) the thin line work of this sheet gave no points at all; 100, 80 and 60 all gave the same six.
River Road is drawn about 35 ft wide against a 61 to 67 ft modern right-of-way; its junctions are measured from the narrower drawn pair.
The two Dempsey Avenue junctions carry about 4 m residuals in the same fit; Dempsey Avenue may have been widened on one side.

50 ft. Undercliff Av., Edgewater Pl., River Road, Dempsey Av. to below Hillard Av. (Hilliard Avenue); Columbia Ter. East and South (Columbia Terrace). One part; 6 auto GCPs with ink_below_paper 100 (default found none).

sheet-9.description: The stretch of Edgewater between Garden Place and the sheet 8 blocks, with the Warner Sugar Refining Company's works on the Hudson River below River Road. The sheet is turned: drawn at 50 ft to an inch, with north pointing to the right (about 66 degrees clockwise of up), so Undercliff Avenue runs across the top, Edgewater Place across the middle and River Road across the lower middle, and the river lies along the bottom. Garden Place crosses the left part diagonally from Undercliff Avenue to River Road between blocks 90 and 89, with the Edgewater Creche for Women and Children beside it; block 93 at the far left and blocks 87, 81 and 80 are laid out in narrow lots, most of them empty, with scattered dwellings, a row of five two storey dwellings (lots J to N) on Undercliff Avenue and the Church of the Holy Rosary at the right edge. Edgewater Place ends at block 87 and does not reach Garden Place. On block 80 along River Road stand syrup tanks of the Warner Sugar Refining Co., the E. G. Kaufer grain and feed store with a hay and feed house and grain elevator, and the Hayek Co. cabinet factory. Several railroad tracks run beside River Road on the river side. Below them, on filled land, the Warner Sugar Refining Co. (block 79) has its pan house, char house and kilns, boiler and power houses, melter house, cooper shop and storage, dry house, shipping house, a barrel bridge and a carpenter shop, with the long raw sugar and refined sugar docks on piles reaching to the exterior pier line; at the lower left (block 88) are the Batterson and Eisele marble works with cutting, sawing, polishing and turning shops and a crane on frame supports. Notes on power, heat and fire protection accompany both works.
notes: Turned sheet: north points to the right, about 66 degrees clockwise of up; the fitted rotation differs from sheet 8's by 90.0 degrees and the scale agrees with it to 1 percent.
Edgewater Place ended at block 87 in 1911; the modern street continues through to Garden Place, so that modern junction is not used.

Placed by the two detected Garden Place junctions (Undercliff Avenue, River Road) and six lot corners matched to modern parcels: four on lots J to N of block 81 on Undercliff Avenue, two on block 80 at Edgewater Place. Modern Edgewater Place parcels sit 2 to 3 m off the drawn street lines.
Per-part settings: ink_below_paper 100 as on sheet 8; River Road given its drawn width of 30 ft, since the modern right-of-way (75 ft) made the detector place the Garden Place junction 8 m off.
Warner Sugar Refining Co. char house drawn from plans and to be sprinklered.

50 ft, turned (north to the right, rotation +66). Undercliff Av., Garden Pl., Edgewater Pl. (ends at block 87), River Road; Warner Sugar Refining Co., Batterson & Eisele marble works. One part; 2 auto Garden Pl. junctions + 6 lot corners matched to modern parcels.

sheet-11.description: The shore of Edgewater around the foot of Edgewater Road, drawn at 50 ft to an inch and turned on the sheet so that north points to the upper right (about 57 degrees clockwise of up). River Road crosses the middle of the sheet from left to right with a pair of railroad tracks along its river side. Above it, Edgewater Road runs across the top from the left edge to its junction with Undercliff Avenue at the upper right, and the short stretch of Edgewater Road from that junction down to River Road (now Archer Street) bounds block 106 on the east and block 105 on the west. Blocks 108 and 106 between Edgewater Road and River Road are large, mostly empty lots with a few dwellings and sheds; block 105 has two dwellings. Below River Road, at the lower left, are the building material and cement yard of O. Meyer (lime and cement and mason material sheds) and the planing mill and lumber yards of E. H. Hinners' Sons with an engine room, office, shavings store house, lumber racks and sheds, beside an open pier on piles that runs out into the Hudson River. The rest of the shore below River Road is a wide bay of open water reaching nearly to the road. At the lower right are a dwelling and sheds and the high pile barrel yards of the Valvoline Oil Co., continued on sheet 10. The exterior line for piers is marked in the river at the bottom.
notes: The short stretch of Edgewater Road from Undercliff Avenue down to River Road is modern Archer Street; the part running west along the top of the sheet is still Edgewater Road.

Placed by the two detected junctions on old Edgewater Road (Archer Street) at Undercliff Avenue and at River Road only, written as a helmert transformation; low confidence. The drawn length between them (341 ft) agrees with the modern one (355 ft) to 4 percent.
Per-part detector setting ink_below_paper 100, as on sheets 8 and 9.

50 ft, turned (north to upper right, rotation +57). Edgewater Rd. (the stretch down to River Road is now Archer Street), Undercliff Av., River Road; E. H. Hinners' Sons planing mill, O. Meyer building materials. One part; helmert on 2 junctions, low confidence.

sheet-14.description: The works of the Corn Products Refining Co. on the Hudson River shore at Shadyside, in the south of Edgewater, drawn at 50 ft to an inch and turned on the sheet so that north points to the upper right; the river lies along the bottom of the sheet. The works are the whole sheet (key number 117). A long range of brick buildings, each with automatic sprinklers, runs down the middle: dextrine house, dry starch house with starch packing and kilns, wet starch house with motors, mills, hoppers and shakers, steep and table house, corn house with corn bins and a steel tank, and on the other side machine shop, steep water house, grinding, oil house with germ presses and dryers, feed house, repair shop and feed dryers, power house with pumps, refinery with copper and tin shop and glucose rooms, kiln rooms, bone ovens and the refining building. An 8 in. fire main runs on the roof of a long conveyor, and a coal conveyor and coal elevator serve a long boiler house with two rows of boilers and two chimneys on the side towards sheet 12. Railroad sidings run along both sides of the works. Two piers reach into the river: shipping piers at the lower left and the coal conveyor pier ending in a hopper and power house. A note block describes the works' fire protection (watchmen, Grinnell sprinklers, supply from the Hackensack Water Co. reservoir, Nordberg and Smith-Vaile pumps). The left edge repeats the north row of the General Chemical Co. works from sheet 16.
notes: No street is drawn on the sheet; the part is placed only by six building and bulkhead corners carried from sheet 16 (General Chemical Co. building 3, the yellow building west of it, and the bulkhead corner at the property line), plus two derived points from the similarity of those six.

All carried points lie along the seam with sheet 16, so position away from that edge (the piers and the boiler house side towards sheet 12) depends on the rotation they give; carried points from sheets 12 or 13 would check it.
Mfrs. of glucose, starch and corn oil.
50 ft. Corn Products Refining Co. works and piers (117); no streets. Turned, north to the upper right. Placed by six corners carried from sheet 16 plus two derived points.

sheet-15.description: Shadyside at the south end of Edgewater, drawn at 50 ft to an inch with north a little anticlockwise of up. River Road runs down the left-centre of the sheet from the top edge, with a bend half way, to the Bergen and Hudson county boundary at the bottom; Gorge Road comes down from the Palisades on its west side and joins it, and Chemical Lane runs east from River Road near the top. West of River Road is lot 115 and the steep slope of the Palisades, with a few frame dwellings and sheds and a vacant, dilapidated dwelling; below the dash-dot county boundary line are Hillside Place and Riverside Place in Hudson County. On River Road at Gorge Road stands a row of frame stores and dwellings with a wagon shed and hall (key number 116). Along Chemical Lane are a row of small two-storey dwellings, a store room, wagon sheds and an open shed. A railroad siding runs down the middle of the sheet between River Road and the works, with a loop track curving east. The east half belongs to the chemical works: the General Chemical Company (diagram from plans, admittance refused; key number 118) at the upper right, and the Barrett Mfg. Co. (key number 120) below it, with barrel storage, barrel shed O, the Davis and Arundell iron foundry, a chemical laboratory, coal pile, tar tanks Nos. 15 and 16 and a storage house. Water pipes of 6 to 30 in. run along River Road and Chemical Lane, with hydrants and a fire alarm box. The bottom margin is marked Hudson County Volume 8a.
notes: River Road here is modern Old River Road (between the county line and Thompson Lane); it is no longer a through road.
Riverside Place is the line of the north part of modern Churchill Road (North Bergen side); Hillside Place and Chemical Lane are not in the modern street data.
Gorge Road has been realigned at its foot; the modern junction with Old River Road lies south of the drawn one.

No street junction survives in usable form. Placed by the drawn corner where the county boundary meets the east edge of River Road (modern county-line vertex) and a fit of the drawn River Road centreline and county line to modern Old River Road and the county boundary (rotation -20.5, 7.95 px/ft, RMS 3.1 m); the other control points are derived from that fit.
The county boundary is drawn along the east edge of River Road south of the corner.

50 ft. River Road (now Old River Road), Gorge Road, Chemical Lane; Hillside and Riverside Pl. below the county line; General Chemical (118), Barrett (120). Placed by the county-line corner and a shape fit of River Road and the boundary.

sheet-16.description: The chemical works on the Hudson River shore at Shadyside, south Edgewater, drawn at 50 ft to an inch with north a little anticlockwise of up; the river is on the right. The upper two thirds is the General Chemical Company works (key number 118; admittance refused, diagram from plans): rod chambers, pyrites burners, acid chambers, a platina still room, nitric and muriatic stills, packing house, ore crusher, sheds, laboratory, a blacksmith shop, and a large dock shed with tanks on the roof and an acid tank on the bulkhead. Railroad sidings curve in from the west across the north of the works. The lower third is the Barrett Mfg. Company (key number 120): tar stills, condensers and boiler house, an open shed, paper storage and a fire-proof reinforced concrete tar paper and roofing factory, tar tanks Nos. 1 to 11 and 15 (up to 17,000 barrels), pitch tanks and pitch cooling shed, naphtha house, gravel bins, lime shed and carpenter shop, blacksmith and pipe shops, machine shop, boiler house, the aqua ammonia factory with anhydrous ammonia cylinders and stills, a Worthington fire pump and a storage house on the shore. A note block gives Barrett's fire protection (watchmen, Grinnell sprinklers in two buildings, city water and suction from the Hudson River). Hydrants and water pipes are marked throughout.
notes: No street is drawn on the sheet. Placed by four points carried from sheet 15 (two building corners of the General Chemical Co. at the top left and two hydrants of the Barrett works at the left), all near the left edge; written as a helmert.
Spencer Kellogg & Sons' stack on this sheet and on sheet 17 differ by about 6.5 m through the two placements before sheet 17 was tied to it.
50 ft. General Chemical Co. (118) and Barrett Mfg. Co. (120) works; no streets. Placed by four points carried from sheet 15 (helmert).

sheet-17.description: The Hudson River shore at Shadyside, the south end of Edgewater, drawn at 50 ft to an inch and turned on the sheet so that north points to the upper right. River Road crosses the top of the sheet, with the Hudson County boundary line drawn along its south-east edge; the land north-west of it is Hudson County and left blank (Hudson County Volume 8a). Below River Road run railroad lines and a siding curving towards the works on sheets 15 and 16, then three works on filled land reaching to the bulkhead and the river: the Bulls Ferry Chemical Co. at the left (key number 122; manufacturers of cotton and silk sizes: galleries, boiler house, mill and dyeing house, store rooms, an office on piles, a vacant steam coil building and open shed for barrels); Pyle's Pearline Works in the middle (key number 121; manufacturers of soap and pearline: buildings Nos. 1 to 6 with drying, crushing, packing and grinding rooms, engine and boiler house, office building) with a pier on piles 500 ft long; and Spencer Kellogg and Sons' mill and elevator at the right (key number 120; manufacturers of linseed oil: a fire-proof mill, seed bins, cake shed with a movable platform and screw conveyor, store rooms, boiler house with a 150 ft stack, tanks) with its own pier. The edge of sheet 16 (Barrett Mfg. Co.) shows at the right. Water pipes and hydrants are marked along River Road and through the works.
notes: River Road here is modern Old River Road; the county boundary still follows its old south-east edge.

No street junction survives. Placed by the kink of the drawn south-east road edge where the boundary turns up the Palisades (modern county-line vertex), a fit of that edge to the modern county boundary (rotation 65.5, RMS 0.8 m), and two points carried from sheets 15 (barrel shed O) and 16 (Spencer Kellogg & Sons' stack); those two disagree with the boundary fit by 3 to 4 m.

50 ft. Turned, north to the upper right. River Road on the Hudson County line; Bulls Ferry Chemical (122), Pyle's Pearline Works (121), Spencer Kellogg & Sons (120). Placed by the county-line corner, the boundary shape and points carried from 15 and 16.
